To give your healthcare API backend reliable releases, you need solid CI/CD pipelines and end‑to‑end browser tests that catch regressions before they reach production. I also delivered a GraphQL API for Daily Ledger that leveraged dataloaders and per‑field caching, slashing home‑screen load time from 3.2 s to 0.9 s and reducing backend costs by 30 %

The riskiest part is the integration of Redis for caching and session management while keeping data consistency under concurrent health‑record accesses; a mis‑configured cache can serve stale or incorrect data, which is unacceptable in healthcare. I will start by defining the critical data flows, writing integration tests for them, and configuring Redis with appropriate eviction policies and TTLs, then lock the whole process into the CI pipeline.

Does a first sprint focused on establishing the CI pipeline, Redis schema, and a handful of high‑priority end‑to‑end tests sound like a good way to de‑risk the project?
